ai.title: Simplify env setup: use .env.local with Bun native loading
ai.summary: Env setup simplified to rely on Bun's native .env loading. .bin/bun wrapper now syncs Infisical secrets directly to .env.local instead of managing a separate .infisical-cache or sourcing direnv. .env.development.local handles worktree overrides with highest precedence. Gitignore updated to exclude .env.local and .infisical-cache. Docs (CONTRIBUTING.md, knowledge.md) reflect the shift from complex Infisical/direnv setup to a simpler cp .env.example .env.local flow for personal dev.

eli5.text: Contributors who want to work on the Codebuff codebase no longer need to install two extra tools (infisical and direnv) or run a multi-step setup just to get their local development environment running with secret keys. Now, after cloning the repo, a contributor only needs to copy a single template file (called.env.example) into place and fill in their own values, which is a one-step process. If someone does want the more advanced team-wide secret syncing, that option still works, but it requires an extra step (allowing direnv), and it is only for team members, not for every personal project. This simplified setup is live today: anyone who pulls the latest code will see the easier instructions in the contributing guide and the removed tools from the required setup list.

ai.title: Convert cleanup-worktree.sh to TypeScript
ai.summary: Replaced `scripts/cleanup-worktree.sh` with `scripts/cleanup-worktree.ts`. New script adds port killing logic, verification checks, and `zod` validation for worktree names. Updates `package.json` to invoke `bun scripts/cleanup-worktree.ts`.

eli5.text: When a developer needs to remove a temporary copy of the project (called a "worktree") that was set up for testing, the cleanup tool now first makes sure no background processes tied to that copy are still running before removing it. It also checks that the copy's name is valid, gives clearer warnings if something is missing or won't delete, and runs a bit faster. This affects anyone on the team who creates and deletes these temporary project copies during development. The change is live today; you would notice it only if you use the cleanup command yourself, since it's an internal developer tool.

ai.summary: Added a test case in `context-pruner.test.ts` to verify pruning of saved run state when total tokens (messages + system prompt) exceed the limit. Includes new fixture `run-state-context-overflow2.json`.

eli5.text: The system now has a new test that checks whether it properly trims down saved conversation history when the total size (including the system instructions) gets too large. The test uses a sample saved state where messages and the system prompt together exceed the limit, confirming the trimming logic handles the combined size correctly. This only affects internal developers maintaining the system, not anyone using it, it just adds more assurance that the trimming feature works as intended.

ai.title: Fix context pruner to pass system prompt and tools
ai.summary: Context pruner now receives system prompt and tool definitions to calculate effective message budget. `AgentState` types in `.agents/types/agent-definition.ts`, `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-definition.ts`, and `common/src/types/session-state.ts` enforce non-optional `systemPrompt` and `toolDefinitions`. `run-agent-step.ts` passes `tools` to pruner, while `spawn-agent-inline.ts` propagates parent system prompt and tools to child agents. `getInitialAgentState` and `createAgentState` initialize these fields to empty string and object respectively.

eli5.text: If you use a long-running agent conversation that keeps lots of past messages, the conversation manager now correctly counts the agent's instructions and available actions when deciding how much room is left for new messages, rather than overlooking them and sometimes chopping too aggressively. This mainly affects multi-step agent runs where a parent assistant spawns helper assistants, because those helpers now inherit the parent's instructions and tool set, and any saved conversation state keeps these fields filled in instead of leaving them blank.

ai.title: Fix agent-runtime test types and mocks
ai.summary: Added missing `tools` and prompt fields to test mocks in `packages/agent-runtime`. Refactored `loop-agent-steps` test to verify `stepsComplete` propagation via generator yield instead of module mocking. Ensures type safety and correct runtime behavior assertions.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the test suite that checks the agent-runtime was updated to add missing fields (tools and prompt) to its test data so the tests match the real system. One specific test was rewritten to verify that when the assistant signals it's done with a step (end_turn), that information correctly travels through the step-running process, without relying on fake module replacements. If you looked at the logs, you'd see fewer type errors and a cleaner passing test that directly confirms the step-completion signal flows through. This is live in the test code today and only affects developers running these tests.

ai.title: Add harder BuffBench eval sets for codebuff, manifold, plane, saleor
ai.summary: New JSON eval datasets and generation scripts added to `evals/buffbench/` targeting complex multi-agent orchestration tasks. Includes `eval-codebuff2.json`, `eval-manifold2.json`, `eval-plane2.json`, and `eval-saleor2.json`. Scripts `main-hard-tasks.ts` and `filter-supplemental-files.ts` facilitate dataset creation. These sets test lightweight orchestrator modes and constrained editor agents against real-world repo modifications.

eli5.text: The team added tougher training tests that teach assistant programs how to edit real software projects more carefully. These new tests are designed to challenge the assistants with trickier, multi-step editing tasks across several popular codebases, so the assistants have to gather information, make changes, and verify their work in a more realistic way. The harder sets are now in place and ready to be used by the tools that evaluate how well the editors work.

This only affects internal requests made through the assistant's websocket connection, so most users won't notice anything different, but the process is a bit more stable now.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.548 ships shared analytics dispatcher and theme link
ai.summary: This release bump to 1.0.548 bundles the shared analytics dispatcher (`createAnalyticsDispatcher` in `common/src/util/analytics-dispatcher.ts`) used by both CLI and Web loggers, along with centralized analytics payload construction in `common/src/util/analytics-log.ts` and structured error logging via `setAnalyticsErrorLogger` in `cli/src/utils/analytics.ts`. It also adds dedicated `link`, `directory`, and `imageCardBorder` theme keys (`cli/src/types/theme-system.ts`, `cli/src/utils/theme-system.ts`) so components like `terminal-link.tsx` and `image-card.tsx` use specific colors instead of generic `theme.info`. Additional user-facing changes include the `.env.local` Bun-native env setup simplification and the `editor-multi-prompt` max-tier agent replacing `editor-best-of-n-opus`.
ai.evidence: Commit 5e02e91e modifies only `cli/release/package.json` (1 line: version 1.0.547 -> 1.0.548), a release-bump with no behavioral change; the release updates list documents what shipped in 1.0.548.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.548 makes the command-line tool look better and its analytics smarter. The biggest change you will see is that links, directories, and image card borders now use their own dedicated colors instead of generic ones, so themes render more consistently across dark and light modes, and markdown hyperlinks and bold inline code display properly. Behind the scenes, a shared analytics dispatcher now handles event tracking for both the CLI and web versions, removing duplicated logic, buffering events correctly, and flushing them only after your user ID is known, which makes error logging more reliable and production tracking uniform. The developer setup was also simplified, switching to Bun's native.env loading so local secrets sync straight to a.env.local file without the old Infisical and direnv complexity, making it easier for contributors to get started. Upgrading gives you a cleaner, more polished terminal look, plus faster and more dependable background analytics and simpler local development.

ai.title: Remove legacy backend package and refactor CLI agent loading
ai.summary: This commit removes the entire legacy backend package, including its Express server, WebSocket implementation, LLM provider adapters, admin tools, and authentication middleware. References to the backend and its environment variables are scrubbed from .env.example, CONTRIBUTING.md, ROADMAP.md, authentication.knowledge.md, common/knowledge.md, common/src/env-schema.ts, codebuff.json, and evals/buffbench/eval-codebuff.json. The CLI now initializes its agent registry via the SDK and refactors MCP client resource handling.
ai.evidence: The diff deletes the entire backend/ directory and removes backend-related references from .env.example, CONTRIBUTING.md, ROADMAP.md, authentication.knowledge.md, common/knowledge.md, common/src/env-schema.ts, codebuff.json, and evals/buffbench/eval-codebuff.json; it also adds initializeAgentRegistry() in cli/src/index.tsx and refactors cli/src/utils/local-agent-registry.ts and common/src/mcp/client.ts.
ai.migration: No migration is required for users of the Freebuff CLI; backend users should migrate to the SDK-based flows.
ai.unknowns: The rollout plan and consumer of the new MCP resource handling are not detailed in the drafts.

changes.what: Deleted the entire legacy backend package, including its server, APIs, LLM adapters, WebSocket implementation, and utilities.
Refactored the local agent registry to load user agents via the SDK and initialized it at startup.
Removed the backend WebSocket client and schema, and refactored the MCP client's resource handling.
Removed unused backend-related environment variables from the evaluation configuration.
Updated documentation to remove backend references and dependencies.

ai.summary: Scripts init-worktree.ts now writes NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL to web/.env.development.local instead of root .env.development.local. CI workflows (npm-app-release-legacy.yml, npm-app-release-prod.yml, sdk-release.yml) removed the global env-overrides for NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_BACKEND_URL to prevent localhost leakage into SDK integration tests. This ensures worktree port overrides apply only to the web package, while SDK tests continue using production backends.

eli5.text: When developers run a local version of the app on their computer, the web browser now loads the Codebuff app settings only for the web part of the project, keeping the rest of the tooling pointed at the production backend. You wouldn't see this yourself, but if you looked at a developer's terminal logs you'd notice the local app URL being written into a separate folder for the web package instead of a shared root file. The same change also stopped one of the backend URLs from being overridden in release testing, so SDK tests keep hitting the real production servers instead of a local address.

ai.title: Hide working indicator during askuser
ai.summary: Status indicator logic in `cli/src/utils/status-indicator-state.ts` now accepts `isAskUserActive`. When true, it forces `kind: 'idle'`, suppressing "working..." and "thinking..." messages. `cli/src/chat.tsx` passes `isAskUserActive: askUserState !== null` to the state calculator. This prevents redundant spinner text while the CLI awaits user input.

eli5.text: When the assistant pauses to ask you a question, the screen no longer shows distracting "working..." or "thinking..." text. Previously, that status text would keep spinning while you were being prompted; now it stays quiet during the pause. You would simply see no animated status line appear while the command waits for your reply. This affects the part of the program that displays status text while you interact with it.

ai.title: Replace editor-best-of-n-opus with editor-multi-prompt agent
ai.summary: New `editor-multi-prompt` agent replaces `editor-best-of-n-opus` in the max-tier agent configuration. It spawns multiple `editor-implementor-opus` agents with distinct strategy prompts, then uses `best-of-n-selector-opus` to choose the optimal implementation. Defined in `.agents/editor/best-of-n/editor-multi-prompt.ts`, it requires an array of short prompts specifying different approaches (e.g., caching vs minimal changes). The base agent prompts in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` are updated to reference this new editor agent for non-trivial code changes.

eli5.text: The assistant now solves coding tasks by trying multiple approaches in parallel instead of one. For bigger, more complex requests, it generates a few different solutions at once and then picks the best result, which should give higher-quality code. You wouldn't directly control this, but the assistant's code changes are likely to be more thorough and reliable than before.
